Coarse-to-fine physics-guided reconstruction of gridded sea level anomalies from HY-2B/C/D altimetry
abstract: The capability of the Chinese HY-2B/C/D altimeter constellation for gridded sea level anomaly (SLA) reconstruction using only HY-2 observations remains insufficiently evaluated. This study presents a physics-guided framework designed for near-real-time (NRT) SLA reconstruction in the Northwest Pacific and retrospectively evaluates it using 2022−2025 HY-2B/C/D observations. The framework combines an OI-derived coarse background with deep-learning refinement, with target-period reconstruction driven solely by HY-2B/C/D along-track data. Validation against an identical set of 1255 independent tide-gauge observations yields mean RMSE of 0.051 m and a mean correlation coefficient (r) of 0.83 over 12 tide-gauge stations. Inter-product comparisons during 2022−2025 show closer agreement with the DUACS DT and NRT products than with NSOAS, although differences in SLA reference conventions and geophysical correction standards among the products should be considered when interpreting regional discrepancies. Scale-dependent evaluation using SARAL/AltiKa along-track observations indicates a mean effective spatial resolution of approximately 300 km. Dynamical consistency is further assessed against surface-drifter observations using geostrophic velocity anomaly magnitude, yielding mean RMSE of 0.181 m s−1 and r of 0.54. These results demonstrate that spatially coherent and dynamically plausible daily SLA fields can be reconstructed with HY-2B/C/D as the sole altimetric observations during the target period, supporting the potential of the proposed framework for NRT SLA reconstruction under sparse observational constraints.

title: Gravity-conditioned diffusion for seafloor bathymetric resolution enhancement
abstract: Global bathymetric products such as SRTM15+ provide extensive ocean coverage but cannot resolve many fine-scale seafloor features captured by shipborne multibeam surveys. Generative reconstruction methods can reconstruct more detailed terrain, but they may also introduce plausible-looking structures that are not supported by observations. We propose GravBathy-Diff, a conditional diffusion framework that uses observed low-resolution bathymetry as its primary input and incorporates satellite-altimetry-derived marine gravity as an auxiliary physical constraint. The gravity-differential enhancement module jointly encodes bathymetry, terrain derivatives, and the co-registered gravity field at the input stage. Gravity-conditioned time–frequency modulation regulates the contribution of gravity across diffusion stages and feature bands, while gravity-guided attention focuses this information on the spatial locations and feature channels where it is most useful. Deflections of the vertical, gravity anomalies, and vertical gravity gradients derived from Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) wide-swath altimetry are compared as alternative conditioning fields. Experiments are conducted on real SRTM15+ –multibeam bathymetry pairs from four ocean regions and assessed using depth error, perceptual similarity, terrain derivatives, and spectral fidelity. GravBathy-Diff achieves the strongest overall performance among the evaluated regression, adversarial, and diffusion methods, with the exception of one regional gradient-RMSE result. It ranks first on all six metrics averaged over four additional ocean areas and remains effective on an independent public digital elevation model (DEM) benchmark at 4×. Among the three gravity representations, the vertical gravity gradient provides the most effective guidance for reconstructing local relief. These results show that marine gravity can support the recovery of fine-scale seafloor structure while reducing high-frequency artifacts that are inconsistent with the available observations.
